name: Badge Counter
hint: Press 98, then +1 twice: the count rolls over into 99+.
description: A count bubble (or a dot) on your own element: wrap an icon, avatar or tab and it sits on its corner. Digits roll like an odometer, the count rolls over into 99+ past the cap, only increases send out a ring, and changes are announced politely.
usage: Wrap the element the count belongs to: <BadgeCounter count={unread} label="Notifications"><IconButton … /></BadgeCounter>. Also put the count in that element's own aria-label ("Notifications, 3 unread"); the badge adds a polite announcement when the count changes. It hides at 0 unless `showZero`; `max` caps the number ("99+"); use `kind="dot"` when the exact number doesn't matter, and `overlap="circle"` on round hosts such as avatars. With no children it renders the bubble inline (a count in a nav row). Also exported: Badge, the bubble alone for any position:relative element.

keyboard.does: Skips the bubble, which takes no focus; focus lands on the element it wraps, whose own name should include the count.

screenReader: The bubble is hidden from assistive technology; the host element you wrap carries its own name, and a polite live region says each change after mount ("`label`: 3", "more than 99", or "new" for a dot). With no host, a hidden text says the current count; `announce={false}` turns the live region off.

dataProps.description: The number to show. The badge follows it; hidden at 0 unless showZero.
Cap: above it the badge reads "max+" (99+).
The element the badge sits on (an icon button, avatar, tab). Omit to render the bubble inline.
A number, or a plain dot when only "something new" matters.
Which corner of the child the badge sits on.
Shape of the child: "circle" pulls the badge in so it sits on a round avatar's edge.
Height of the badge: sm 16px (on a small avatar or a tab), md 20px, lg 24px (on a large tile). The digits are 60% of it. A number sets the height in px exactly.
What is being counted, used in the announcement ("Notifications: 3"). Without it only the number is announced.
Announce count changes in a polite live region (never on mount). Turn off when the host's own label already updates and is announced.
Show the gallery's three sample hosts (bell, messages, avatar) with buttons to change the count. Leave off in real UI.
The wrapper element around your child and the badge.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the root <span>. className and style are merged with the component's own.
